title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions

draft.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
card: Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the heat energy taken in or given out by a reaction at constant pressure. It is measured in kJ, or kJ/mol.
a reaction that releases heat to the surroundings. The products have less energy than the reactants, so ΔH is negative. The surroundings get warmer.
a reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings. The products have more energy than the reactants, so ΔH is positive. The surroundings get cooler.
The sign of ΔH is from the point of view of the reaction system. Heat leaving the system gives a negative sign. Heat entering gives a positive sign.
draft.remember: Exothermic: heat out, ΔH negative. Endothermic: heat in, ΔH positive.

a.q: A student mixes two solutions in a beaker. The beaker feels cold, and the thermometer reading falls. What does this show about the reaction?
opts: It is endothermic, and ΔH is positive
It is endothermic, and ΔH is negative
It is exothermic, and ΔH is positive
It is exothermic, and ΔH is negative
a.why: The surroundings got colder, so the reaction absorbed heat from them. That makes it endothermic, with a positive ΔH. A cold beaker does not mean a negative ΔH, because the sign describes the energy change of the reaction, not the feel of the beaker.
a.clue: Where did the heat go: into the reaction or out of it?

b.q: Burning natural gas in a stove heats a pot of water. The reaction has ΔH = -890 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?
opts: The products have less energy than the reactants
The reaction absorbs 890 kJ of heat per mole
The products have more energy than the reactants
The reaction is endothermic, as it gets very hot
b.why: A negative ΔH means heat is released, so the products hold less energy than the reactants. The option about absorbing 890 kJ is tempting because of the number, but absorbing heat would give a positive ΔH.
b.clue: Look at the sign of ΔH, not the size of the number.

a.best: It is endothermic, and ΔH is positive

b.best: The products have less energy than the reactants
